name: David Lewis
bio: David Lewis (1683?–1760) was a poet and editor, a friend of Alexander Pope, who edited the anthology Miscellaneous Poems by Several Hands (1726). His own Miscellaneous Poems appeared in 1730.
The lines here, addressed to Pope in the years of the Dunciad quarrels, were printed in 1732.

poems.title: When none shall rail
poems.author: David Lewis
poems.collection: Pieces Published on Occasion of the Dunciad (1732)
poems.text:
While Malice, Pope, denies thy Page
It's own celestial Fire;
While Critics, and while Bards in Rage
Admiring, won't admire;

While wayward Pens thy Worth assail,
And envious Tongues decry,
These Times tho' many a Friend bewail,
These Times bewail not I.

But when the World's loud praise is thine,
And Spleen no more shall blame,
When with thy Homer Thou shalt shine
In one establish'd Fame,

When none shall rail, and ev'ry Lay
Devote a Wreath to Thee;
That Day (for come it will) that Day
Shall I lament to see.
